title: Left, Root, Right Tree Walk
statement:
Given the root of a binary tree, list its values in in-order: for every node, first everything in its left subtree, then the node itself, then everything in its right subtree.

Return the values as an array. An empty tree gives [].

The recursive version is three lines. Interviewers usually follow up by asking for a version without recursion, so be ready to write that too.

examples.why: This is a search tree, and in-order on a search tree reads the values in sorted order.
1 has no left child, so it comes first. 2's left child 3 comes before 2.

hints: Write down the definition: in-order of a tree = in-order of the left subtree, then the root, then in-order of the right subtree. That is already a recursive function.
To drop recursion, replace the call stack with your own stack. What does the call stack hold at the moment you visit a node?
Push nodes while walking left as far as possible. Pop one, record it, then move to its right child and repeat the walk-left step.

explain.intuition:
Recursion matches the definition directly: visit the left subtree, record the node, visit the right subtree.

The iterative version makes the hidden call stack visible. When the recursive version records a node, the stack holds that node's ancestors whose left subtree is still being visited. So walk left from the current node, pushing every node you pass. When you can't go left any more, the top of the stack is the next node to record. Pop it, record it, and then do the same walk-left starting from its right child. Each node is pushed once and popped once. It works like a DOM tree walker that keeps its own stack of open parents.
steps: Set cur = root and an empty stack.
While cur is not null or the stack is not empty:
Walk left: while cur is not null, push it and set cur = cur.left.
Pop a node, append its value to the output.
Set cur to that node's right child and continue the loop.
pitfalls: Recording the node when you push it instead of when you pop it. That gives pre-order, not in-order.
Ending the loop when the stack is empty but cur still points to a right subtree. The loop condition needs both checks.
Relying on recursion for very deep trees. A chain of 100 000 nodes overflows the default stack in both JavaScript and Python.

solutions.title: Recursion
solutions.idea: Left subtree, node, right subtree, exactly as defined.

solutions.title: Explicit stack
solutions.idea: Push the path while walking left; pop to record; then continue from the popped node's right child.

solutions.title: Morris walk (no stack)
solutions.idea: Before going left, link the rightmost node of the left subtree back to the current node. Following that link later returns you to the parent; remove it on the way back.

followups: Write pre-order and post-order iteratively too. Which one is the hardest, and why?
Turn the iterative version into an iterator with next() and hasNext() that uses O(h) memory.
